blocks.text: EXCLUSIVE: After a decade-long effort to secure the film rights to I Never Promised You a Rose Garden — Joanne Greenberg ’s classic 1964 novel, which she calls “one of the most arresting and authentic explorations of mental illness ever written” — Ashley Avis has done it.

links.text: I Never Promised You a Rose Garden

blocks.text: The rising filmmaker, whose credits include Disney+’s Black Beauty , will direct from her own script and produce alongside Edward Winters through her Winterstone Pictures banner.

Inspired by Greenberg’s experiences as a young woman diagnosed with schizophrenia, I Never Promised You a Rose Garden follows Deborah Blau, a brilliant and deeply troubled Jewish teenager who retreats into an elaborate kingdom she has constructed within her own mind.

blocks.text: As Deborah loses her grip on reality, she’s admitted to Chestnut Lodge, where she forms an unlikely bond with renowned German psychiatrist Dr. Clara Fried, whose own past remains shrouded in unresolved trauma and mystery. In the years following World War II, these two women must navigate the fragile boundary between reality and fantasy, forging a unique relationship that challenges the fabric of mental health as we know it.

Regarded as a seminal work on mental health, I Never Promised You a Rose Garden has sold millions of copies worldwide and previously inspired an Academy Award-nominated 1977 film, directed by Anthony Page and starring Kathleen Quinlan.

Avis told us of the novel, “Joanne Greenberg crafted a story that is at once deeply intimate and breathtakingly imaginative, because it is courageously personal. She invites us into the Kingdom of Yr, into all of its seduction, and beauty along with its violence – and we will question, along with Deborah, whether it is possible to give it up.”

What moved Avis most about the book “was the true story tucked between the pages of Rose Garden; the relationship between two very real women who inspired these characters. Deborah Blau and Dr. Fried become mirrors for one another as they navigate darkness, trauma, healing, and the question of what it means to truly live in, and accept, reality.”

A great lover of animals — and horses, in particular — Avis channeled that passion into the two films for which she’s best known: a Disney+ adaptation of Anna Sewell’s classic 1877 novel Black Beauty , starring Kate Winslet and Mackenzie Foy, and the Critics Choice Award-nominated documentary Wild Beauty: Mustang Spirit of the West . Currently, Avis is developing American Wolf — a film on the wolves of Yellowstone, based on the novel by Nate Blakeslee — with Appian Way. Additionally, she has set up a reimagining of Wim Wenders’ romance City of Angels at Warner Bros. She is represented by CAA and Ryan Goodell of Yorn, Levine, Barnes.
